For each of three rows, write colour 9 to four bytes at $D8F8,Y and four at $D90C,Y. Y starts at zero and advances by 40 after each row; the counter at $9888 ends at zero. With I/O visible, these are colour RAM writes. The next setup continues at $9346.

Call $77E0 with the message pointer selected by the preceding path, then fall through to the mode and countdown initializer at $9369. The ordinary label path loads $953F; earlier branches can supply other pointers. The message callback was stubbed in the controlled tests.

Store 0 in the shop mode byte at $9533, store $DC in the countdown at $9537, and fall through to the wait path at $9373. Starting from 0, the captured left and right handlers keep the mode among $FF, $00 and $01 if no other code changes it.

Call $3C2A, decrement the shop countdown at $9537 and branch to $93A6 when it becomes zero. Otherwise call $370B, $94AA and $9497; on set carry, repeat this path. On clear carry, fall through to $9386. Starting from the initialized $DC and holding the tested branches, zero is reached after 220 calls to $3C2A.
Call $3C2A, decrement $9537 and branch to $93A6 at zero. Otherwise call $370B, $94AA and $3C4C, then fall through to the sampled-input choice at $9397.

Use the sampled active-low inputs: if $70 is zero, branch to the shop gate at $93FA; otherwise, if $73 is zero, branch to the left handler at $93BC; otherwise, if $74 is zero, branch to the right handler at $93DA. When all three are nonzero, jump back to $9386. The preceding code calls $3C4C to sample joystick port 2; fire takes priority over left, and left over right.
